seats.oldValue: There was hope in the air that Wednesday.
seats.newValue: The sun was shining and the day was warm.
seats.execution: No sun or warm weather is mentioned anywhere in the passage. Lines 1 to 3 give the cause: the scents of plumcakes, jellies and gravy make it impossible to feel altogether gloomy.

seats.oldValue: That it is hard to forgive the loss of the book.
seats.newValue: The next time the girls go skating.
seats.execution: 'Next time' comes from Amy's complaint at line 49, outside the window. At line 53 Meg says 'Go after them' now, and lines 53 and 54 have Amy wait only till Jo has got good-natured with Laurie.

seats.newValue: Jo to be friends with her again.
seats.execution: True at line 55, and it is what Meg says will follow Amy's kiss, not the moment to wait for. Lines 53 and 54 have Amy wait till Jo has got good-natured with Laurie, then take a quiet minute.

seats.oldValue: Until Laurie has gone off home and left them alone.
seats.newValue: Laurie to go off home and leave them alone.
seats.execution: Lines 53 and 54 tell Amy to wait until Jo has got good-natured with Laurie, then take a quiet minute. The child supplies a different, likely condition, Laurie going home, which Meg never gives.

redrafts.value: Three: with Mrs Hurst, Miss Bingley and Miss Bennet.
redrafts.execution: A third dance with Miss Bennet is supplied; she dances with Mr Bingley at lines 60 and 61 and never with Mr Darcy.

rebuilds.why: Sweep R1037: the too-wide option carried en-attribute-transfer, whose hint does not fit a vocabulary sense; retagged en-vocab-neighbouring-sense. The walk script counts five people, who are listed on lines 22 and 23, outside the cited 17 to 21; the window is widened to 17 to 23 (the sentence the walk script reads ends on line 23), stem and lineRefs together.

stem.text: Read lines 17 to 23. Line 21 says: 'when the party entered the assembly-room'. What does 'party' mean here?

options.value: A celebration with food, music and games.
options.execution: A birthday party is the sense a child meets first, and the word sits in a sentence about a ball.

options.value: The ball that Mr Bingley talked of giving at Netherfield.
options.execution: Mr Bingley talks of giving a ball at Netherfield at line 38, later in the passage, and the child carries that party-like event back to line 21. At line 21 'party' is the group that entered the assembly-room, counted at lines 21 and 22 as five people.

options.value: A group of people who arrive together.
A team that people vote for in an election.
options.execution: The political sense, a side that people vote for, is a real second sense of 'party'. Line 21 rules it out: the party 'entered the assembly-room', and lines 21 to 22 count it as 'only five altogether'.

options.value: Everybody who came to the assembly that night.
options.execution: 'Party' can also mean everyone at a social gathering, a real sense of the word, but too wide here. Line 21 fixes a smaller group: the party 'entered the assembly-room', and lines 21 to 23 count it as 'only five altogether'.

rebuilds.why: Sweep R1037: the key (14 words, the only long qualified option) gave itself away by length. Shortened to 10 words, using only what lines 21 to 23 give, so the walk script's 'two sisters, a husband, a young man' still reaches it.

stem.text: Read lines 17 to 23. Who actually came into the assembly-room with Mr Bingley?

options.value: His five sisters and a cousin.
options.execution: Five sisters and a cousin is line 20, the SECOND report. True, inside the window, and the wrong element for a question about who actually walked in.

options.value: Twelve ladies and seven gentlemen.
options.execution: Twelve ladies and seven gentlemen is the first report, at lines 17 and 18, inside the window. The child takes the first thing the village heard, where the stem asks who actually walked in, which lines 21 and 22 give as five people.

options.value: His two sisters, Mr Hurst and Mr Bennet.
options.execution: One name changed: Mr Bennet for the young man. Everything else matches line 22.

options.value: His two sisters and both their husbands.
options.execution: Only one husband is named — 'the husband of the eldest' at line 22 — and a second is supplied.

options.value: His two sisters, one sister's husband and a young man.

rebuilds.why: Sweep R1037: the key was the only two-part option and the longest (15 words). Key shortened to 10 words, and the en-plausible-not-stated distractor recast with a matching two-part shape (10 words), so neither shape nor length singles out the key.

stem.text: When Mr Darcy first walked in, the room thought very well of him. Read lines 26 to 30. Why?

options.value: Because he danced with lots of different ladies.
options.execution: Dancing every dance is Mr Bingley at line 37, carried across to Mr Darcy, who dances twice. In the window, line 27 answers the stem: 'drew the attention of the room by his fine'.

options.value: Because he was friendly and kind to everyone he met.
options.execution: Friendliness and kindness are nowhere in lines 26 to 30. Line 32 finds him proud and above his company, and line 40 has him decline being introduced to any other lady.

options.value: Because he was the tallest man in the room.
options.execution: 'The tallest man in the room' is the absolute version of line 27's 'fine, tall person'.

options.value: Because he was handsome and people heard he was rich.
Because he owned a large estate in Derbyshire.
options.execution: The Derbyshire estate is line 33, and it appears only when the room has turned against him. In the window, line 27 answers the stem: 'drew the attention of the room by his fine'.

rebuilds.why: Sweep R1037: the walk script never reached the key and leaned toward the sauce distractor. Its last sentence is replaced so it ends on the key.

stem.text: Look at lines 41 to 43. What does 'relish' on line 43 mean there?

options.value: the enjoyment she took in the taste
a sauce eaten along with the food
options.execution: A real sense, and line 43 makes this a word about how she ate rather than what.

options.value: the speed at which she ate up her half of it
options.execution: That is rapidity at line 43, joined to this word by as well as, so they differ.

explanationPatch.walkScript: Read line 43 and find the two words joined by as well as. One of them is rapidity, which is about speed. Relish is the other way she ate it. So relish is about how much she enjoyed the taste.
explanationPatch._previousWalkScript: Read line 43 and find the two words joined by as well as. One of them is rapidity, which is about speed. The other has to be about something else, and the puff is what she is eating.

rebuilds.why: Sweep R1037: the hint said three people are named in lines 38 to 42; only two are named and five come up. Hint replaced with a true statement that still points at who is advising whom.

stem.text: Look at lines 38 to 42. What does Miss Jenkyns recommend to Boz?

options.value: That he take Dr Johnson's style as a model.
That her father take Boz for a model.
options.execution: Line 38 has her father recommending Johnson to her, so this turns the two round.

options.value: That he form his own style upon her letters.
options.execution: True at line 39 of HER, and it is what she did rather than what she advises.

options.value: That he stop publishing his work in numbers.
options.execution: True at line 35, outside this window; lines 38 to 42 say nothing about numbers.

explanationPatch.hintCore: Several people come up in these lines. Work out who is giving advice to who.
explanationPatch._previousHintCore: Three people are named in these lines. Work out who is advising whom.

notes.ENG-002-pp-05: Fault: too-wide option tagged en-attribute-transfer (hint does not fit) and walk script used lines outside 17 to 21. Fix: retagged en-vocab-neighbouring-sense with a new execution; stem and lineRefs now cite lines 17 to 23, where the five-person sentence ends.
notes.ENG-002-pp-06: Fault: length giveaway on the key. Fix: key shortened to 'His two sisters, one sister's husband and a young man.' (10 words, distractors 5 to 8); nothing else changed.
notes.ENG-002-pp-09: Fault: key the only two-part option and the longest. Fix: key now 'Because he was handsome and people heard he was rich.' (10 words); 'spoke kindly' distractor recast two-part as 'Because he was friendly and kind to everyone he met.' (same tag); options now 8 to 10 words.
notes.ENG-002-pp-12: Fault: execution cited line 63 for Miss Bennet dancing with Mr Bingley. Fix: execution redraft now cites lines 60 and 61.
notes.ENG-012-ML-01: Fault: 'There was hope in the air that Wednesday.' read as a possible second answer through the colon on line 3. Fix: seated 'The sun was shining and the day was warm.' (en-plausible-not-stated); the passage never mentions weather.
notes.ENG-012-ML-08: Fault: walk script never reached the key. Fix: walk script now ends 'So relish is about how much she enjoyed the taste.'; old text kept under _previousWalkScript.
notes.ENG-025-LW-09: Fault: three distractors could not complete 'wait for', so grammar singled out the key. Fix: each recast as something Amy could wait for: 'The next time the girls go skating.' (retagged en-wrong-scope-retrieval, line 49), 'Jo to be friends with her again.' (en-within-span-wrong-element, line 55), 'Laurie to go off home and leave them alone.' (same tag, same execution). Stem unchanged.
notes.ENG-017-CR-09: Fault: hint claimed three people are named in lines 38 to 42 (untrue). Fix: hint now 'Several people come up in these lines. Work out who is giving advice to who.'; old text kept under _previousHintCore.
